question: What is the GST rate on fresh milk and pasteurised milk under HSN 0401?
reference_answer: Fresh milk and pasteurised milk (not concentrated nor containing added sugar) under HSN 0401 are exempt from GST (0% rate).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 2/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Entry 25: Fresh milk and pasteurised milk under HSN 0401 attracts NIL (0%) GST.

question: What is the GST rate on laptops and automatic data processing machines under HSN 8471?
reference_answer: Automatic data processing machines, laptops, and personal computers under HSN 8471 attract 18% GST (9% CGST + 9% SGST or 18% IGST).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Schedule III, Entry 360: Automatic data processing machines under heading 8471 attract 18% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on gold jewellery under HSN 7113?
reference_answer: Articles of jewellery of precious metal (gold, silver, platinum) under HSN 7113 attract a special rate of 3% GST (1.5% CGST + 1.5% SGST or 3% IGST).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Schedule V, Entry 13: Articles of jewellery of precious metal attract 3% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on rough diamonds under HSN 7102?
reference_answer: Rough diamonds under HSN 7102 attract a concessional GST rate of 0.25% (0.125% CGST + 0.125% SGST or 0.25% IGST).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25 Jan 2018: Rough diamonds under heading 7102 attract 0.25% GST.

question: What was the GST rate on medicaments (HSN 3004) before 22 September 2025 and what is the rationalized rate after that date?
reference_answer: Prior to 22 September 2025, medicaments under HSN 3004 were taxed at 12%. Effective 22 September 2025 (56th GST Council recommendations), the rate was rationalized to 5%.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-CT(Rate) Schedule II Entry 63 (12%); 56th GST Council Meeting Recommendations rationalized to 5% w.e.f. 22 Sep 2025.

question: What is the GST rate on pre-packaged and labelled rice under HSN 1006?
reference_answer: Pre-packaged and labelled rice under HSN 1006 attracts 5% GST (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST). Unbranded, loose rice is exempt (0%).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 6/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13 July 2022: Pre-packaged and labelled rice under heading 1006 attracts 5% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on IT software consulting and development services under SAC 9983?
reference_answer: Information technology software development, design, and consulting services under SAC 9983 attract 18% GST (9% CGST + 9% SGST or 18% IGST).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Section 5, Heading 9983: Other professional, technical and business services attract 18% GST.

question: Are education services provided by an educational institution to its students exempt from GST?
reference_answer: Yes, education services provided by an educational institution to its students, faculty, and staff under SAC 9992 are completely exempt from GST (0%).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Entry 66: Services provided by an educational institution to its students, faculty and staff are exempt.

question: What is the GST rate on healthcare services provided by clinical establishments or doctors under SAC 9993?
reference_answer: Healthcare services by a clinical establishment, an authorised medical practitioner, or paramedics under SAC 9993 are exempt from GST (0%).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Entry 74: Healthcare services by a clinical establishment or authorised medical practitioner are exempt.

question: What is the GST rate on restaurant service (standalone restaurants without alcohol) under SAC 9963?
reference_answer: Restaurant services provided by standalone restaurants (without alcohol and not located in a hotel with room tariff >= ₹7,500) attract 5% GST without input tax credit.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 46/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 14 Nov 2017: Supply of restaurant service attracts 5% GST with no ITC.

question: What is the GST rate on motor cars for personal transport under HSN 8703?
reference_answer: Under HSN 8703, motor cars historically attracted 28% GST plus compensation cess (ranging from 1% to 22%). Post-22 Sep 2025 rationalization, luxury/demerit vehicles fall under the 40% slab.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-CT(Rate) Schedule IV Entry 166 (28%); 56th GST Council Meeting rationalized luxury slab to 40%.

question: What is the GST rate on smartphones and cellular telephones under HSN 8517?
reference_answer: Smartphones and mobile phones under HSN 8517 attract 18% GST (increased from 12% to 18% w.e.f. 1 April 2020).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 03/2020-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25 March 2020: Telephones for cellular networks or for other wireless networks attract 18% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on air conditioning machines under HSN 8415 after 22 September 2025?
reference_answer: Air conditioning machines under HSN 8415 attract 18% GST following the rate rationalization effective 22 September 2025 (reduced from 28%).
supporting_passage: 56th GST Council Meeting Recommendations: Air conditioning machines under 8415 reduced from 28% to 18% slab w.e.f. 22 Sep 2025.

question: What is the GST rate on legal services provided by an advocate to a business entity?
reference_answer: Legal services provided by an individual advocate or firm of advocates to a business entity attract 18% GST, payable under reverse charge mechanism (RCM) by the recipient business.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Entry 2: Legal services provided by an advocate to a business entity are subject to RCM at 18%.

question: What is the GST rate on hotel accommodation where room tariff is ₹1,000 or less per day?
reference_answer: Hotel accommodation where the value of supply of a unit of accommodation is up to ₹1,000 per day attracts 12% GST (exemption was withdrawn w.e.f. 18 July 2022).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 4/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13 July 2022: Hotel rooms up to ₹1,000/day brought into the 12% GST bracket.

question: What is the GST rate on beauty and skincare preparations under HSN 3304 post-September 2025?
reference_answer: Beauty and cosmetic preparations under HSN 3304 attract 18% GST following the rationalization from the 28% slab effective 22 September 2025.
supporting_passage: 56th GST Council Meeting Recommendations: Cosmetic and skincare preparations under 3304 rationalized to 18%.

question: What is the GST rate on household soaps under HSN 3401?
reference_answer: Soap and organic surface-active products in the form of bars or cakes under HSN 3401 attract 18% GST.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Schedule III, Entry 54: Soap under heading 3401 attracts 18% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on coffee beans (not roasted or decaffeinated) under HSN 0901?
reference_answer: Unroasted and non-decaffeinated coffee beans under HSN 0901 attract 5% GST.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Schedule I, Entry 31: Coffee, whether or not roasted or decaffeinated attracts 5% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on tea under HSN 0902?
reference_answer: Tea (whether or not flavoured) under HSN 0902 attracts 5% GST.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Schedule I, Entry 32: Tea under heading 0902 attracts 5% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on cane or beet sugar in solid form under HSN 1701?
reference_answer: Cane or beet sugar in solid form under HSN 1701 attracts 5% GST.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Schedule I, Entry 91: Sugar under heading 1701 attracts 5% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on commercial general construction services under SAC 9954?
reference_answer: General commercial construction services under SAC 9954 attract 18% GST (9% CGST + 9% SGST) with full input tax credit on inputs.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Heading 9954: Construction services for commercial buildings attract 18% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on economy class air travel under SAC 9964?
reference_answer: Transport of passengers by air in economy class under SAC 9964 attracts 5% GST with limited input tax credit (on input services).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Heading 9964: Air passenger transport in economy class attracts 5% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on business class air travel under SAC 9964 post-September 2025?
reference_answer: Business class air passenger transport under SAC 9964 attracts 18% GST following rationalization (previously 12%).
supporting_passage: 56th GST Council Meeting Recommendations: Air passenger transport in other than economy class rationalized to 18%.

question: What is the GST rate on banking and financial services (processing fees, annual charges) under SAC 9971?
reference_answer: Banking and financial services such as loan processing fees, card maintenance charges, and account fees under SAC 9971 attract 18% GST.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Heading 9971: Financial and related services attract 18% GST.

question: What is the GST rate on aerated and carbonated soft drinks under HSN 2202 post-September 2025?
reference_answer: Aerated drinks containing added sugar or flavour under HSN 2202 attract 40% GST under the demerit/luxury rationalized slab.
supporting_passage: 56th GST Council Meeting: Demerit aerated sweetened drinks rationalized to the 40% rate slab.

question: What is the GST rate on exercise books and student notebooks under HSN 4820 post-September 2025?
reference_answer: Exercise books, notebooks, and student registers under HSN 4820 attract 5% GST (rationalized from 12%).
supporting_passage: 56th GST Council Meeting Recommendations: Educational stationery and notebooks under 4820 rationalized to 5%.

question: What is the GST rate on packaged drinking water in 20-litre jars under HSN 2201?
reference_answer: Packaged drinking water in bottles or 20-litre cans under HSN 2201 attracts 18% GST.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 1/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Schedule III, Entry 24: Waters, including mineral and aerated waters under 2201 attract 18%.

question: What is the GST rate on two-wheelers with engine capacity up to 350cc under HSN 8711 post-September 2025?
reference_answer: Motorcycles and two-wheelers with engine capacity not exceeding 350cc under HSN 8711 attract 18% GST (rationalized from 28%).
supporting_passage: 56th GST Council Meeting: Commuter two-wheelers under 350cc rationalized from 28% to 18% slab.

question: What is the GST rate on fresh potatoes, tomatoes, and onions?
reference_answer: Fresh or chilled potatoes (HSN 0701), tomatoes (HSN 0702), and onions (HSN 0703) are completely exempt from GST (0%).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 2/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Entries 36, 37, 38: Fresh vegetables under Chapter 07 attract NIL GST.

question: What is the GST rate on real estate commercial leasing services under SAC 9972?
reference_answer: Renting or leasing of commercial immovable property under SAC 9972 attracts 18% GST with input tax credit available to commercial tenants.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), Heading 9972: Real estate services involving leasing or renting attract 18% GST.

question: What is the statutory due date for filing monthly GSTR-1?
reference_answer: Monthly GSTR-1 is due on the 11th day of the month succeeding the tax period under CGST Rule 59(1).
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 59(1): The details of outward supplies in FORM GSTR-1 shall be furnished on or before the eleventh day of the month succeeding the tax period.

question: What is the statutory due date for filing monthly GSTR-3B?
reference_answer: Monthly GSTR-3B is due on the 20th day of the month succeeding the tax period under CGST Rule 61(1).
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 61(1): Every registered person shall furnish return in FORM GSTR-3B on or before twentieth day of the month succeeding such tax period.

question: What is the due date for quarterly GSTR-1 under the QRMP scheme?
reference_answer: For taxpayers opted into the QRMP scheme, quarterly GSTR-1 is due on the 13th day of the month following the end of the quarter (CGST Rule 59(2)).
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 59(2) & Notif. 83/2020-CT: GSTR-1 for quarterly filers under QRMP is due on the 13th of the month succeeding the quarter.

question: What are the due dates for quarterly GSTR-3B under the QRMP scheme?
reference_answer: Quarterly GSTR-3B under QRMP is due on the 22nd or 24th day of the month following the quarter end, depending on the taxpayer's State/UT.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 83/2020-Central Tax: GSTR-3B quarterly due date is 22nd (Category 1 States) or 24th (Category 2 States) of the following month.

question: What is the due date for filing the annual return in Form GSTR-9?
reference_answer: The annual return in Form GSTR-9 is due on or before 31st December following the close of the financial year under Section 44 of the CGST Act.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 44: Every registered person shall furnish an annual return on or before the thirty-first day of December following the end of such financial year.

question: What is the due date for GSTR-6 filed by Input Service Distributors (ISD)?
reference_answer: GSTR-6 for Input Service Distributors is due on the 13th day of the month succeeding the tax period under CGST Rule 65.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 65: Input Service Distributor return in FORM GSTR-6 shall be furnished on or before thirteenth day of the succeeding month.

question: What is the due date for GSTR-7 filed by TDS deductors under GST?
reference_answer: GSTR-7 for TDS deductors is due on the 10th day of the month succeeding the month in which deduction was made under CGST Rule 66.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 66: Return in FORM GSTR-7 for TDS deductors shall be submitted on or before tenth day of the month following deduction.

question: What is the due date for GSTR-8 filed by E-commerce operators collecting TCS?
reference_answer: GSTR-8 for E-commerce operators collecting TCS is due on the 10th day of the month following the month in which tax was collected under CGST Rule 67.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 67: Statement in FORM GSTR-8 by e-commerce operators shall be filed on or before tenth day of the following month.

question: What is the due date for GSTR-5 filed by Non-Resident Taxable Persons?
reference_answer: GSTR-5 is due on the 20th day of the month succeeding the tax period or within 7 days after expiry of registration under CGST Rule 62.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 62: Return for Non-Resident Taxable Persons in FORM GSTR-5 is due on 20th of the month following the period.

question: What is the due date for GSTR-4 filed by composition scheme taxpayers?
reference_answer: GSTR-4 annual return for composition taxpayers is due on or before 30th April following the end of the financial year (CGST Rule 62(1)(ii)).
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 62: Composition taxpayers furnish annual return in FORM GSTR-4 on or before 30th day of April following the financial year.

question: When is the monthly tax payment challan PMT-06 due for the first two months of a quarter in QRMP?
reference_answer: Under the QRMP scheme, tax for the first two months is deposited via challan PMT-06 by the 25th day of the succeeding month.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 84/2020-Central Tax: Tax payment for M1 and M2 in QRMP shall be deposited on or before the 25th day of the next month using Form GST PMT-06.

question: What is the due date for using the Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) in QRMP?
reference_answer: The optional IFF facility for uploading B2B invoices in months 1 and 2 of a quarter is available from the 1st to the 13th day of the succeeding month.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 59(2): Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) is available between the 1st and 13th day of the succeeding month.

question: What is the due date for GSTR-1 for the tax period of September 2024?
reference_answer: For monthly filers, GSTR-1 for September 2024 was due on 11th October 2024.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 59(1): Due date is 11th of succeeding month (11 October 2024).

question: What is the due date for GSTR-3B for the tax period of September 2024?
reference_answer: For monthly filers, GSTR-3B for September 2024 was due on 20th October 2024.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 61(1): Due date is 20th of succeeding month (20 October 2024).

question: What is the due date for GSTR-9 for the financial year 2023-24?
reference_answer: GSTR-9 annual return for FY 2023-24 is due on 31st December 2024 under Section 44 of the CGST Act.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 44: Due date is 31st December following the financial year end.

question: What turnover threshold exempts registered persons from mandatory filing of GSTR-9 annual return?
reference_answer: Taxpayers whose aggregate turnover in a financial year is up to ₹2 crore are exempt from the mandatory filing of Form GSTR-9.
supporting_passage: Notification No. 10/2022-Central Tax & Notif. 14/2024-CT: Annual return GSTR-9 is waived for taxpayers with AATO up to ₹2 crore.

question: What is the turnover threshold for filing reconciliation statement Form GSTR-9C?
reference_answer: Self-certified reconciliation statement in Form GSTR-9C is mandatory for registered persons whose annual aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 80(3): Every registered person whose aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore shall submit a self-certified reconciliation statement in FORM GSTR-9C.

question: What is the deadline for claiming Input Tax Credit for a financial year?
reference_answer: Under Section 16(4) of the CGST Act, ITC for an invoice/debit note can be claimed up to 30th November following the end of the financial year, or the date of furnishing annual return, whichever is earlier.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 16(4) as amended by Finance Act 2022: ITC deadline is 30th November following the end of the financial year.

question: What is the deadline to issue credit notes for outward supplies made during a financial year?
reference_answer: Credit notes for supplies made in a financial year must be declared on or before 30th November following the end of the financial year (Section 34(2)).
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 34(2): Credit note details shall be declared on or before 30th day of November following the financial year.

question: Can GSTR-3B be filed without prior filing of GSTR-1 for the same period?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 39(10) and Rule 59(6), a registered person is barred from furnishing GSTR-3B if GSTR-1 for the relevant tax period has not been furnished.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 39(10) & Rule 59(6): GSTR-3B filing is blocked if preceding GSTR-1 is unfiled.

question: What is the due date for GSTR-1 for quarter ending December 2024 under QRMP?
reference_answer: For Q3 (October–December 2024), GSTR-1 under QRMP is due on 13th January 2025.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 59(2): GSTR-1 QRMP due on 13th of month following quarter end.

question: What is the due date for GSTR-10 (Final Return) upon cancellation of GST registration?
reference_answer: Form GSTR-10 (Final Return) must be filed within 3 months of the date of cancellation or the date of the cancellation order, whichever is later (Section 45).
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 45: Final return in FORM GSTR-10 is due within 3 months of cancellation date or cancellation order.

question: What is the due date for CMP-08 quarterly payment statement by composition dealers?
reference_answer: CMP-08 quarterly tax payment statement is due on the 18th day of the month succeeding the end of each quarter (CGST Rule 62).
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 62: Statement containing details of payment of self-assessed tax in FORM GST CMP-08 is due on 18th of the following month.

question: What happens if the GST return due date falls on a public holiday?
reference_answer: Under the General Clauses Act Section 10, if the statutory due date falls on a Sunday or gazetted public holiday, the return may be filed on the next working day without late fees.
supporting_passage: General Clauses Act, 1897 Section 10; CBIC clarification on court holidays and bank holidays.

question: Can a taxpayer rectify errors in GSTR-1 after 30th November of the succeeding financial year?
reference_answer: No. Under proviso to Section 37(3), no rectification of error or omission in GSTR-1 is allowed after 30th November following the end of the financial year.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 37(3) proviso: Rectification cut-off date is 30th November following the end of the financial year.

question: What are the four primary statutory conditions to claim ITC under Section 16(2)?
reference_answer: Under Section 16(2): (1) Possession of tax invoice/debit note; (2) Invoice details reported by supplier in GSTR-1 and reflected in recipient's GSTR-2B; (3) Actual receipt of goods or services; (4) Tax actually paid to the Government; and (5) Filing of return under Section 39.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 16(2): Mandatory conditions (a) to (d) including clause (aa) for GSTR-2B matching.

question: Is input tax credit available on purchase of motor vehicles for personal or passenger transport under Section 17(5)?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(a), ITC is blocked on motor vehicles for transportation of persons having approved seating capacity up to 13 persons, unless used for further supply of vehicles, passenger transport, or driving school training.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(a): Blocked credits on passenger motor vehicles seating <= 13 persons with specific exceptions.

question: Can a business claim ITC on food and beverages or outdoor catering provided to employees?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(b)(i), ITC on food and beverages and outdoor catering is blocked, unless it is obligatory for an employer to provide it under an active statutory law (e.g. Factories Act).
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(b)(i): ITC blocked on food, beverages and outdoor catering unless statutory obligation.

question: Is ITC available on works contract services for construction of a commercial office building?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(c), works contract services for construction of immovable property are blocked, except when used for construction of plant and machinery, or where supplied as an input service for further works contract.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(c): Works contract services for construction of immovable property (other than plant and machinery) are blocked.

question: Can a company claim ITC on goods or cement purchased for construction of a factory building on its own account?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(d), ITC is blocked on goods or services received by a taxable person for construction of an immovable property (other than plant or machinery) on his own account, even when used in business.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(d): ITC blocked on goods/services used for construction of immovable property on own account.

question: What is the formula under CGST Rule 42 to reverse common input tax credit attributable to exempt supplies?
reference_answer: Under Rule 42(1)(m), the reversal amount D1 is calculated as: D1 = (E / F) * C2, where E is exempt turnover in the State, F is total turnover in the State, and C2 is the common input tax credit.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 42(1)(m): D1 = (E/F) * C2 attributable to exempt supplies.

question: How is common credit C2 defined under Rule 42?
reference_answer: C2 is defined as C1 - T4, where C1 is eligible credit after deducting exclusive personal (T1), exempt (T2), and blocked (T3) credits from total ITC (T), and T4 is credit exclusively used for taxable supplies.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 42(1): C1 = T - (T1+T2+T3); C2 = C1 - T4.

question: What is D2 in Rule 42 and how is it computed?
reference_answer: Under Rule 42(1)(j), D2 represents the deemed reversal of common credit attributable to non-business or personal use, calculated as 5% of common credit C2 (D2 = 0.05 * C2).
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 42(1)(j): D2 = 5% of C2 for non-business purpose reversal.

question: Is input tax credit available on goods lost, stolen, destroyed, or written off?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(h), input tax credit is blocked on goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or disposed of by way of gift or free samples.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(h): ITC blocked on goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or given as gift/samples.

question: What is the useful life of capital goods assumed under Rule 43 for ITC reversal?
reference_answer: Under CGST Rule 43(1)(c), the useful life of capital goods is taken as 60 months (5 years) from the date of the invoice.
supporting_passage: CGST Rule 43(1)(c): The useful life of capital goods shall be taken as sixty months from the date of invoice.

question: Is tax paid under reverse charge mechanism (RCM) eligible for input tax credit?
reference_answer: Yes. Tax paid by the recipient under RCM (Section 9(3) or 9(4)) is 100% eligible as ITC in the same month, provided the underlying supply is used in the course or furtherance of business.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 16(1) & Section 9(3)/(4): Tax paid on reverse charge basis is credited to electronic credit ledger.

question: What is the consequence if a recipient fails to pay the supplier within 180 days from the invoice date?
reference_answer: Under the second proviso to Section 16(2), the recipient must reverse the ITC availed along with interest under Section 50. The credit can be reclaimed once the payment is made to the supplier.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 16(2) second proviso & Rule 37: Mandatory ITC reversal if supplier not paid within 180 days.

question: Is input tax credit available on corporate gym or health club memberships for employees?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(b)(ii), ITC is explicitly blocked on membership of a club, health, and fitness centre.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(b)(ii): ITC blocked on membership of a club, health and fitness centre.

question: Is input tax credit available on purchases made from a supplier registered under the Composition Scheme?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(e), tax paid on goods or services supplied by a person paying tax under Section 10 (composition levy) is not available as ITC.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(e): ITC blocked on goods or services on which tax has been paid under section 10.

question: Is ITC available on taxes paid in evasion or fraud cases under Section 74, 129, or 130?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(i), any tax paid in accordance with the provisions of Sections 74 (fraud/wilful misstatement), 129 (detention), and 130 (confiscation) is blocked from ITC.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(i): ITC blocked on any tax paid in accordance with sections 74, 129 and 130.

question: What is the statutory order of utilization for IGST credit?
reference_answer: Under Section 49(5) and Rule 88A, IGST credit must first be utilized completely against IGST liability; any remaining balance can be utilized towards CGST and SGST/UTGST in any order and proportion.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 49(5) & Rule 88A: IGST credit utilization order rules.

question: Can CGST credit be utilized to pay SGST liability?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 49(5)(e) and (f), CGST credit can never be cross-utilized to discharge SGST liability, and SGST credit cannot discharge CGST liability.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 49(5)(e)/(f): Cross-utilization between CGST and SGST is prohibited.

question: Is ITC available on free samples or business promotional gifts distributed to dealers?
reference_answer: No. Under Section 17(5)(h), ITC on goods disposed of by way of gift or free samples is specifically blocked from ITC.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(5)(h): ITC blocked on goods disposed of by way of gift or free samples.

question: Can a banking company opt for a 50% flat ITC credit under Section 17(4)?
reference_answer: Yes. Under Section 17(4), a banking company or financial institution can opt to avail an amount equal to 50% of eligible ITC every month, with the remainder lapsing, in lieu of Rule 42 apportionment.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 17(4): Option for banking companies to avail 50% of the input tax credit every month.

question: If a registered person sells plant & machinery on which ITC was taken, how is tax determined under Section 18(6)?
reference_answer: Under Section 18(6), the taxpayer must pay an amount equal to the ITC availed reduced by 5 percentage points per quarter or the tax on the transaction value, whichever is higher.
supporting_passage: CGST Act Section 18(6) & Rule 44(6): Sale of capital goods on which ITC taken requires repayment based on useful life or transaction tax.

question: What is the late fee per day for delay in filing a NIL GSTR-3B return?
reference_answer: Under Notification No. 19/2021-Central Tax, the late fee for a NIL GSTR-3B return is ₹20 per day (₹10 CGST + ₹10 SGST), subject to a maximum cap of ₹500 (₹250 CGST + ₹250 SGST).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 19/2021-Central Tax, dated 01 Jun 2021: Nil return late fee is ₹20/day capped at ₹500.

question: What is the maximum late fee cap for GSTR-3B for a taxpayer with annual turnover up to ₹1.5 crore having tax liability?
reference_answer: For taxpayers with AATO up to ₹1.5 crore having tax liability, late fee is ₹50 per day (₹25 CGST + ₹25 SGST), capped at a maximum of ₹2,000 (₹1,000 CGST + ₹1,000 SGST).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 19/2021-Central Tax: Non-nil return AATO up to ₹1.5 Cr capped at ₹2,000.

question: What is the maximum late fee cap for GSTR-3B for a taxpayer with annual turnover between ₹1.5 crore and ₹5 crore?
reference_answer: For taxpayers with AATO between ₹1.5 crore and ₹5 crore having tax liability, late fee is ₹50 per day, capped at a maximum of ₹5,000 (₹2,500 CGST + ₹2,500 SGST).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 19/2021-Central Tax: AATO ₹1.5 Cr to ₹5 Cr capped at ₹5,000.

question: What is the maximum late fee cap for GSTR-3B for a taxpayer with annual turnover exceeding ₹5 crore?
reference_answer: For taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding ₹5 crore, late fee is ₹50 per day, capped at a maximum of ₹10,000 (₹5,000 CGST + ₹5,000 SGST).
supporting_passage: Notification No. 19/2021-Central Tax: AATO exceeding ₹5 Cr capped at ₹10,000.
